plan.notes: Source: official NJIT 2026-2027 catalog page 'B.S. in Computer Science' (https://catalog.njit.edu/undergraduate/computing-sciences/computer-science/bs/), 'Plan of Study Grid' -- "The program requires the completion of a minimum of 120 credits. The following plan of study illustrates a typical path to completion." Catalog year 2026-2027 (site header 'Catalog 2026-2027'; the live current catalog, not an archive edition). Transcription method: fetched the page HTML with curl and manually transcribed every grid row (course code, title, credits, footnote markers) on 2026-09-30; per-term sums re-verified against the catalog's printed Term Credits (14/14, 15/16, 15/16, 15/15 = 120). Caveats: (a) The catalog's grid does not list per-course prerequisites, so all prereq arrays are intentionally empty -- no prerequisites invented; the published term ordering preserves the prerequisite chain. (b) FYS SEM (First-Year Student Seminar) is a required 0-credit course (required_zero). (c) The catalog notes this curriculum is the maximum recommended credits per semester (full-time load = 12 credits), and that first-year students are placed in a curriculum that positions them for success which may result in additional time to complete requirements -- students should consult academic advisors. (d) The degree may be earned with an optional concentration (Cybersecurity and Privacy; AI: Learning and Reasoning; AI: Systems and Infrastructure), completed within the existing elective slots of this plan -- not transcribed as a separate plan. (e) Grade requirements per catalog: B or better expected in CS 100; C or better in all CS courses that serve as prerequisites of required courses; 2.7 GPA required for co-op enrollment.

courses.title: General Elective
courses.choice_note: General Elective (catalog footnote 1): any 3-credit course except a course already required for the program or any course covering prerequisite material for first-semester courses. Rules on Electives (catalog footnote 2): students pursuing a concentration must select electives to satisfy concentration requirements; at most 6 credits from CS 485/DS 485/IS 485/IT 485 Special Topics may count (at least 3 must be CS 485 if 6 used; only approved CS 485 topics count toward concentrations); at most 3 credits from YWCC 310/410/411 Co-OP courses may count toward general electives; the following cannot count as electives: Computing Literacy GER, ENGL 099, PHYS 102, MATH 105, MATH 107, MATH 226, MATH 244, MATH 326, MATH 341, DS 340, IS 331.
